Rashi on Pesachim 111b:10:1.english: And it is found in the shadow of a sea squill - [The] sea squill with which Joshua demarcated the Land for Israel.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:10:2.english: That has not grown a cubit - Which has not grown a cubit.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:11:2.english: While his feet are wet - While his feet are moist from the water of washing.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:12:1.english: Hanging in the house - One who hangs his bread in the air inside a basket.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:12:2.english: He hangs his basket - his basket, with bread inside it.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:13:1.english: The angel of food - An angel appointed to provide sustenance.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:13:2.hebrew: נקוד שמיה - לשון נקידו, כמו מנקד חצירו; לפיכך אינו רוצה שיהו פרורים נשלכים לידרס ברגל:
Rashi on Pesachim 111b:13:2.english: Nakud is his name - [This is] an expression of cleanliness, like "one who cleans his courtyard"; therefore he does not want crumbs to be thrown [down] to be trampled underfoot.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:13:3.english: The angel of poverty is called Naval - And perhaps he enters a house where he sees that they do not observe a practice of cleanliness with bread.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:13:5.english: [He] is afraid - and he does not know why.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:1:1.english: One who relieves himself on the stump of a palm tree:

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:1:2.hebrew: האי מאן דמפני אגירדא דדיקלא אחדא ליה רוח פלגא - פלשדי"ן (פליישי"ן: שיתוק) בלע"ז:
Rashi on Pesachim 111b:1:2.english: One who relieves himself on the stump of a palm tree, a spirit of palga seizes him - Palashdin (palaisin: paralysis) in Old French.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:1:3.english: Tzerada - Pain of half the head.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:1:4.hebrew: אי מיקטל קטיל - אם נקצץ האילן, נהרג האיש; ואם נעקר האילן, האיש מת:
Rashi on Pesachim 111b:1:4.english: If it is cut down, he is killed - If the tree is cut down, the man is killed; and if the tree is uprooted, the man dies.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:1:5.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr> הני מילי היכא דלא מנח כרעיה עילויה כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 111b:1:5.english: This is the reading: "This applies where he does not place his foot upon it, etc."

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:2:1.english: There are five shadows - For an evil spirit rests beneath them.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:2:2.english: The shadow of kanda - [This is] the name of the tree.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:2:3.hebrew: טולא דפרחא - צלף, קרפי"ף בלע"ז:
Rashi on Pesachim 111b:2:3.english: The shadow of a caper-bush - [That is,] a caper-bush, karpif in Old French.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:2:4.english: Zeradata - *Sorbier* [Old French for the sorb tree].

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:2:5.english: The shadow of an arba - A ship.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:2:6.english: The shadow of a willow - The shadow of a willow tree.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:2:7.english: [And any tree] whose silveih is hard - Its wood.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:4:1.english: [Those] of the caper-bush [are] ruchei - That is their name.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:4:2.english: [Those] near the sorb trees - Shedim is their name.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:4:3.hebrew: דבי איגרי - המצויין בגגות, רשפי שמם:
Rashi on Pesachim 111b:4:3.english: Of the roofs - Those [demons] found on roofs, their name is rishfei.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:4:4.hebrew: ונפקא מינה - לכתוב קמיעא בשם אילן, כגון: אם הוזק תחת בי פרחא, יכתוב לו קמיעא בשם רוחי:
Rashi on Pesachim 111b:4:4.english: And the practical difference - [is] to write an amulet in the name of these [demons]; for example, if one was harmed under a caper-bush, he writes an amulet for him in the name of ruḥei.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:5:1.hebrew: למאי נפקא מינה לגזויי לה - לברוח מפניה, לפי שאין לה עינים ואינה רודפתו:
Rashi on Pesachim 111b:5:1.english: What is the practical difference? To flee from it - To flee from it, because it has no eyes and does not pursue him.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:5:2.english: He avoided it - He fled from it.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:5:3.hebrew: כי אזלא נפקא אדיקלא - כשהלכה אחריו, נתקלה ונפלה על עיקר אילן:
Rashi on Pesachim 111b:5:3.english: When it went, it came upon a palm tree - When it went after him, it stumbled and fell upon the trunk of a tree.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:5:4.hebrew: ה"ג פקעה היא וצווח דיקלא - יבש הדקל:
Rashi on Pesachim 111b:5:4.english: This is the reading: "[it] burst and the palm tree dried out" - The palm tree dried out.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:7:1.english: Bar kasha - The watchman of the city.

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:7:2.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>, סודרא דמר דומה כי צורבא מרבנן:
Rashi on Pesachim 111b:7:2.english: This is the reading: "The scarf of [the] Master resembles [that of] a Torah scholar."

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:7:3.english: We have examined the master; he does not know how to say Barukh - For he does not know [how] to recite the blessing over the scarf, "Blessed [are You...] Who crowns Israel."

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:8:1.english: Bachasha - The spoon of the pot [i.e., a ladle].

Rashi on Pesachim 111b:8:2.english: And revolves in a jug of kamkha - [It] revolves inside a jug of kutach.

Tosafot on Pesachim 111b:12:1.hebrew: תליא בביתא קשי לעניותא - מכאן קשה לרש"י, דפירש בפרק קמא דחגיגה (דף ה.): "היינו דאמרי אינשי: זוזי לתליתא שכיחא, לעללא לא שכיח", ופי' לתליתא — לקנות פת לצורך היום, שתולין בסל. ואין דרך לתלותו בסל, דהא אמרינן הכא דקשי לעניותא. ור"ת מפרש שם: לתליתא — כשדוחקין אותו לפרוע, מוצא לווין; אבל לקנות תבואה לאכול, אינו מוצא לווין:
Tosafot on Pesachim 111b:12:1.english: Hanging [food] in the house causes poverty - From here there is a difficulty with Rashi, who explained in the first chapter of Chagigah (5a): "This is what people say: coins for hanging [telita] are readily available; for produce [alala] they are not readily available," and he explained "for hanging" [to mean] to buy bread for the day's need, which people hang in a basket. Yet it is not the practice to hang it in a basket, for here we say that it causes poverty. And Rabbeinu Tam explains there: "For hanging" — when [creditors] press him to pay [a debt], he finds lenders; but to buy grain to eat, he does not find lenders.

Tosafot on Pesachim 111b:9:1.hebrew: ואזיל רב פפא מימיניה - מצדד איצדודי הוה, דאמר בפרק הממונה (יומא דף לז.): "המהלך לימין רבו הרי זה בור":
Tosafot on Pesachim 111b:9:1.english: "And Rav Pappa was walking on his right" - He was walking slightly off to the side, for it is said in the chapter [entitled] HaMemuneh (Yoma 37a): "One who walks to the right of his teacher is an ignoramus."
